extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) evaluating U.S. patent subject matter eligibility under MPEP/Alice-Mayo framework
extracted.subtask_description: Index of subject-matter-eligibility examples used to spot issues and guide application of the Alice/Mayo framework (MPEP 2106), showing which examples require which analyses (Step 2A prongs, Step 2B) and what considerations are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Type (Statutory Category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify the claim as a Process or Product (Composition of Matter, Manufacture, and/or Machine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for issue spotting across examples; column heading 'Claim Type aka Statutory Category' (Process / Product (Composition of Matter, Manufacture, and/or Machine)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial Exception — Abstract Idea
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify whether the claim recites an abstract idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract idea is one of the judicial exceptions listed in the index and is further subdivided into groupings (mathematical concepts; mental process; certain methods of organizing human activity). Examples are marked to show which recite abstract ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial Exception — Law of Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify whether the claim recites a law of nature (natural principle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a distinct judicial exception used to categorize examples and determine applicable analysis steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial Exception — Product of Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify whether the claim recites a product of nature limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to flag examples and to trigger Markedly Different Characteristics (MDC) analysis where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial Exception — Multiple exceptions in same claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify when a claim recites multiple judicial exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples are annotated to indicate when more than one exception is recited in the same claim for analysis purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial Exception — No recited exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify claims that do not recite any judicial exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such examples are indicated and typically do not proceed through exception-centered prong analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis Type — Detailed Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform the full, detailed subject matter eligibility analysis for a claim example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Column heading 'Detailed Analysis' indicates examples where a full, step-by-step analysis is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis Type — Streamlined Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the streamlined (MPEP 2106) presentation of Step 2A/2B analyses (Step 2A Prong One, Prong Two; Step 2B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index shows which examples include a streamlined analysis and which of the following sub-analyses apply: Step 2A Prong One (Generally), Step 2A Prong One (Markedly Different Characteristics analysis), Step 2A Prong Two (Exception Integrated Into A Practical Application), Step 2B (Generally), and Step 2B (Claim is eligible because it provides an Inventive Concept).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2A Prong One — Generally
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the claim limitation(s) recite a judicial exception under the general Step 2A Prong One analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For examples issued after the June 2020 revision, the analysis references abstract-idea groupings in MPEP 2106(a)(2); for earlier examples (1–36) the rationale may rely on direct comparisons to judicial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2A Prong One — Markedly Different Characteristics (MDC) analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: For nature-based product (NBP) limitations, assess whether the claimed NBP has markedly different characteristics compared to its natural counterpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index identifies which examples discuss MDC analysis. When to perform MDC analysis: (1) claim focused on NBP limitation(s) so MDC analysis is performed; (2) process claim not focused on NBP (general rule in MPEP 2106.04(c)(I)(c) applies) so no MDC analysis; (3) process claim focused on NBP because exception to general rule in MPEP 2106.04(c)(1)(c) applies so MDC analysis is performed. Characteristics evaluated in MDC analysis include chemical or physical property; function or activity; phenotype; structure or form. Also identifies whether claim recites a single NBP limitation, a combination/mixture of components, or multiple NBP limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2A Prong Two — Exception Integrated Into A Practical Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the judicial exception is integrated into a practical application such that the claim does not seek to tie up the exception itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears as a distinct Streamlined Analysis column heading. For Examples 1–36, the Step 2A Prong Two analysis can sometimes be extrapolated from the existing Step 2B analysis (minus WURC considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2B — Generally
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the additional claim elements, individually or as an ordered combination, provide an inventive concept that transforms the exception into patent-eligible subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index indicates which examples proceed to Step 2B and includes the particular reasoning when a claim is found eligible under Step 2B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2B — Claim is eligible because it provides an Inventive Concept
rubrics_metrics.description: The conclusion that a claim is subject-matter-eligible at Step 2B because the claim provides an inventive concept beyond the judicial exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples are flagged where Step 2B supports eligibility; index distinguishes those conclusions in the 'Streamlined Analysis' column.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration — Improvements to Functioning of a Computer or Other Technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether claimed elements improve the functioning of a computer or other technology, supporting eligibility at Prong Two or Step 2B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among the 'Considerations Discussed in Step 2A Prong Two and/or Step 2B' and used as a positive indication of practical application/inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration — Particular Treatment or Prophylaxis (Prong Two only)
rubrics_metrics.description: For medical/therapeutic claims, assess whether the claim recites a particular treatment or prophylaxis (relevant only at Prong Two).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed explicitly as a Prong Two-only consideration in the index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration — Particular Machine
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the claim is tied to a particular machine in a meaningful way (supporting eligibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the index as a consideration for Prong Two/Step 2B analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration — Particular Transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the claim effects a particular transformation of an article or material (supporting eligibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among considerations used in Prong Two/Step 2B analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration — Other Meaningful Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify other meaningful limitations beyond mere recitation of an exception that tie the claim to application (supporting eligibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index flags when examples rely on limitations that meaningfully limit the exception in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration — Mere Instructions To Apply An Exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect whether additional elements are simply instructions to apply the judicial exception (negative for eligibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as an adverse consideration in Step 2A Prong Two/Step 2B analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration — Insignificant Extra-Solution Activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify additional claim elements that are insignificant extra-solution activities (do not confer eligibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the index as a factor weighing against eligibility in Prong Two/Step 2B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration — Field of Use and Technological Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the claimed field of use and technological environment to determine practical application or lack thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a contextual factor in Step 2A Prong Two/Step 2B analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration — Well-Understood, Routine, Conventional (WURC) Activity (Step 2B only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether additional elements are well-understood, routine, and conventional (a WURC finding weighs against Step 2B inventive concept).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index notes WURC is applicable at Step 2B; Explanatory Notes caution that for Examples 1–36 (pre-June 2020) the WURC conclusion may not be supported by one of the MPEP 2106.07(a)(III) options (1)-(4) now required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration — No additional elements, so no Prong Two or Step 2B analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim contains no additional elements beyond the exception, prong-two/Step 2B analysis does not proceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly listed in the index; such examples are flagged as having no additional elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract Idea Groupings
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify abstract ideas into groupings: Mathematical Concepts; Mental Process; Certain Methods of Organizing Human Activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The index maps example numbers to abstract-idea groupings; 'Mathematical Concepts' is further described as mathematical relationships, formulas/equations, and calculations; 'Mental Process' as concepts performed in the human mind; 'Certain Methods of Organizing Human Activity' includes fundamental economic principles/practices, commercial or legal interactions, managing personal behavior or relationships or interactions between people. For post-June 2020 analyses, Step 2A Prong One explanations should reference MPEP 2106(a)(2) abstract-idea groupings rather than only comparisons to prior judicial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markedly Different Characteristics (MDC) — NBP Limitation Types
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify whether the claim recites a single nature-based product (NBP) limitation, a combination/mixture of multiple components, or multiple NBP limitations (affects MDC analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index lists which examples involve single vs combination vs multiple NBP limitations and whether MDC analysis is performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: MDC — Characteristics Evaluated
rubrics_metrics.description: When performing MDC analysis, evaluate chemical or physical property; function or activity; phenotype; and structure or form to determine whether a product is markedly different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index enumerates these characteristics as the primary categories to be assessed in MDC analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Perform MDC Analysis (process vs product claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for performing MDC analysis depending on whether the claim is process-focused or focused on NBP limitations and whether the MPEP exception to the general rule applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claim is focused on NBP limitation(s), perform MDC analysis. If process claim is not focused on NBP (general rule MPEP 2106.04(c)(I)(c)), do not perform MDC analysis. If process claim is focused on NBP because the exception in MPEP 2106.04(c)(1)(c) applies, perform MDC analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of June 2020 MPEP 2106 Revision to Examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how the June 2020 revision to MPEP 2106 affects the issued examples (1–36 issued prior to that revision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Examples 1–36, the Step 2A Prong One analysis in MPEP 2106 will differ from the analysis presented in the issued examples for abstract-idea identifications: post-revision, the rationale should point to abstract idea groupings in MPEP 2106(a)(2). For Examples 1–36, Step 2A Prong Two can be extrapolated from existing Step 2B analysis (minus WURC consideration); some of these examples would now be eligible at Step 2A Prong Two and a specific list of affected examples is provided (Examples now eligible at Step 2A Prong Two: 3, 4, 21(claim 2), 23(claim 4), 25, 29(claims 5 and 6)). Examples where the result is unchanged but that would require analysis under Step 2A Prong Two are also listed (e.g., 6, 7, 8, 21(claim 1), 22, 23(claims 2 and 3), etc.). Explanatory Notes also flag that WURC conclusions for pre-June 2020 examples may not meet the current MPEP 2106.07(a)(III) support options (1)-(4).
